text: Angelos Postecoglou (/ˈændʒ ˌpɒstəˈkɒɡluː/ ANJ POS-tə-KOG-loo; born 27 August 1965) is a soccer manager and former player who was most recently the head coach of Premier League club Nottingham Forest. Born in Nea Filadelfeia, a suburb of Athens, Greece, Postecoglou was born to a family that migrated from the Alaşehir district of Manisa during the 1923 population exchange between Turkey and Greece. After his father, Dimitris ("Jim"), lost his business following the 1967 Greek military coup, the family moved to Australia in 1970 when Postecoglou was five years old. He grew up in Melbourne, Victoria, and at age 10, his parents changed his surname to "Postekos" due to a trend among Greeks to shorten names at the time, though he legally retains Postecoglou. Postecoglou began playing for South Melbourne Hellas at age nine and played 193 games in the National Soccer League from 1984 to 1993, contributing to their 1984 and 1990–91 titles, the latter as captain in a penalty shootout win over Melbourne Croatia. He was coached by Hungarian Ferenc Puskás, whose 4–3–3 formation with rigid full-backs and attacking wingers influenced Postecoglou’s own coaching style, though he later used attacking full-backs in an inverted position. A knee injury ended his NSL career at age 27. He was named starting left back in South Melbourne's team of the century in 2000 and played four senior international games for Australia between 1986 and 1988, including a debut on 3 August 1986 against Czechoslovakia and appearances in both legs of the 1988 Trans-Tasman Cup, which Australia won 4–1 on aggregate. He also represented Australia at youth level in 1985. After retiring, Postecoglou served as an assistant coach at South Melbourne under Jim Pyrgolios and Frank Arok, becoming head coach in 1996 after Arok’s firing. He led South Melbourne to consecutive National Soccer League titles in 1997–98 and 1998–99, and won the 1999 Oceania Club Championship, qualifying for the 2000 FIFA Club World Championship. He stepped down from South Melbourne in 2000 to become coach of Australia’s youth teams, where he helped identify and develop players, though he was replaced in February 2007 after Australia failed to qualify for the 2007 FIFA U-20 World Cup. He worked as a football pundit for Fox Sports and as an elite consultant to Football Federation Victoria. Postecoglou coached Panachaiki in the Greek third division and Whittlesea Zebras in Melbourne while running coaching clinics. On 16 October 2009, he was appointed head coach of Brisbane Roar, replacing Frank Farina. He released several players and acquired others, including Tommy Oar, Michael Zullo, and Adam Sarota, who moved to Utrecht, and striker Sergio van Dijk to Adelaide United. The 4–0 win against Adelaide United in round 13 was widely praised. Postecoglou led the Roar to the Premiership and Championship in the 2010–11 season, winning the Grand Final 4–2 on penalties against Central Coast Mariners in front of 52,168 people at Lang Park, going on a 36-game unbeaten run and losing only one game all season. He signed a two-year extension until the 2013–14 season on 18 March 2011. In the 2011–12 season, Brisbane Roar became the first team to win back-to-back A-League championships, and Postecoglou became the most successful Australian domestic football coach with four national titles. He announced his resignation as head coach of Brisbane Roar on 24 April 2012 after two-and-a-half years. On 26 April 2012, he signed a three-year contract with Melbourne Victory as head coach. His first game was a 2–1 loss to Melbourne Heart, and his first win came against Adelaide United in Round 4. The following year, Melbourne Victory reached the A-League Preliminary Final after beating Perth Glory 2–1 in an Elimination Final. Postecoglou was appointed head coach of the Australia national team on 23 October 2013, replacing Holger Osieck, tasked with regenerating a team seen as overly reliant on the 2006 Golden Generation. In his first match, a friendly against Costa Rica, Australia won 1–0 thanks to a goal from Tim Cahill. For the 2014 FIFA World Cup, Australia was drawn in Group B with Spain, the Netherlands, and Chile, losing to Chile 3–1 and the Netherlands 3–2, and finishing with a 3–0 loss to Spain, but their competitive performances led to belief in a new Golden Generation. In 2015, Australia won the AFC Asian Cup by defeating Kuwait 4–1 and Oman 4–0, beating China 2–0 in the quarter-final and the United Arab Emirates 2–0 in the semi-final, and winning the final 2–1 after extra time against South Korea. On 22 November 2017, two weeks after qualifying for the 2018 FIFA World Cup, Postecoglou announced his resignation as Socceroos coach. On 19 December 2017, he was appointed head coach of Yokohama F. Marinos, beginning after the 2017 Japanese Emperor's Cup. His first domestic game ended in a 1–1 draw against Cerezo Osaka. After a difficult start, he guided the club to the J-League Cup final and a 12th-place finish in the league. He extended his contract with Yokohama after receiving interest from the Greece national team. In 2019, he won the J1 League with Yokohama F. Marinos, securing their first title in 15 years. On 10 June 2021, Postecoglou became head coach of Scottish Premiership club Celtic, signing a 12-month rolling contract, making him the first Australian manager to coach a major European club. Celtic had just lost their league title to Rangers for the first time in a decade and had not hired English manager Eddie Howe. His first game was a 1–1 draw against FC Midtjylland in a UEFA Champions League qualifier, followed by a 2–1 loss in the second leg, leading to elimination. He lost his first league game 2–1 away to Heart of Midlothian on 31 July. On 19 December 2021, Celtic won the Scottish League Cup after defeating Hibernian 2–1 at Hampden Park. On 2 February 2022, a 3–0 win over Rangers put Celtic at the top of the league for the first time in the season, ending a 13-game unbeaten start for opposing manager Giovanni van Bronckhorst. The league title was sealed on 11 May with a 1–1 draw at Dundee United. Postecoglou won the Scottish League Cup a second time in February 2023 after beating Rangers 2–1 in the final. Celtic ended the 2022–23 season with a record eighth domestic treble after winning the Scottish Cup at Hampden Park against Inverness Caledonian Thistle on 3 June. He was named a candidate for The Best FIFA Football Coach after winning the domestic treble. On 6 June 2023, Postecoglou was appointed head coach of Tottenham Hotspur, starting 1 July on a four-year contract, becoming both the first Australian and first Greek to manage in the Premier League. After an unbeaten start to the 2023–24 season with two wins and a draw in his first three matches, he won the Premier League Manager of the Month award for August, becoming the first manager since David Wagner to win it in his first month. On 24 September, he became the first Tottenham manager to earn points from Arsenal away at the Emirates Stadium in four years, after a 2–2 draw. After continuing the unbeaten streak for a second month, he won the September Manager of the Month award, becoming the first ever manager to win it in each of his first two months. On 1 October, he guided Spurs to their first victory against Liverpool in five years, winning 2–1 at home. On 23 October, he achieved his seventh victory in his ninth league game with a 2–0 win over Fulham. He broke the record for most points earned by a Premier League manager in their first nine games, accumulating 23 points and surpassing Guus Hiddink’s 22 from Chelsea in the 2008–09 season. Postecoglou led Tottenham to three consecutive wins and the league's top spot in October, winning Manager of the Month for a third consecutive time, becoming the first manager to win the award for the first three months of a single season. On 6 November, he suffered his first defeat as Tottenham manager in a 4–1 home loss to Chelsea, during which his side was reduced to nine men after a straight red card to Cristian Romero and a second yellow card to Destiny Udogie. The loss began a five-game winless streak, during which the club drew one match and lost the rest, dropping from first to fifth. Leading Tottenham to an unbeaten run in their first ten games contributed to Postecoglou winning Manager of the Year honours at the London Football Awards on 29 February 2024. However, Tottenham was unable to recapture their strong season start.

Postecoglou, who grew up in Melbourne, Victoria, played Australian rules football from a young age and became a lifelong supporter of the Carlton Football Club in the Australian Football League (AFL), as well as of Liverpool and AEK Athens. He married his first wife, Georgia, in December 1988 and had a son from that marriage; he is currently married to a Georgia, who worked as a marketing manager at South Melbourne during his tenure there, and they have two sons together. His father, who died in 2018, worked hard every day to provide opportunities for Ange to have a better life, and Postecoglou stated that his motivation as a manager is to produce teams his father would enjoy watching. Postecoglou is fluent in Greek and is a Greek Orthodox Christian, and he is often referred to as "Big Ange" or mononymously as Ange or Angie in the media. In November 2022, he was inducted into the Football Australia Hall of Fame for his contributions to Australian football. In a 2018 interview, he cited Paul Keating as his favorite Australian Prime Minister and quoted him during the post-match press conference of the 2025 UEFA Europa League final, saying, "After an unlikely victory, this is one for the true believers." Postecoglou began his managerial career with South Melbourne, Brisbane Roar, Yokohama F. Marinos, Celtic, and Tottenham Hotspur, and also coached Australia U17 and Australia U20. From Chelsea in the 2008–09 season, Postecoglou guided Tottenham to three consecutive wins and the league's top spot in October, earning him Manager of the Month for a third consecutive time, making him the first manager to win the award for the first three months of a single season. On 6 November, he suffered his first defeat as Tottenham manager in a 4–1 home loss to Chelsea, following a straight red card to Cristian Romero and a second yellow card to Destiny Udogie, marking the start of a five-game winless streak where they drew one match and lost the rest, dropping from first to fifth. His leadership contributed to winning Manager of the Year at the London Football Awards on 29 February 2024, following an unbeaten run in their first ten games. However, a 4–2 loss to Liverpool on 5 May marked the club's first four-game league losing streak in 20 years, and despite the poor form, Tottenham finished fifth, qualifying for the 2024–25 UEFA Europa League after a year-long absence from European football. Prior to the 2024–25 season, Postecoglou stated in an interview that he usually wins things in his second year, though after a 1–0 loss to Arsenal on 15 September, he clarified, "I'll correct myself – I don't usually win things, I always win things in my second year. Nothing's changed. I've said it now. I don't say things unless I believe them," which many in the media interpreted as a promise of a trophy. The campaign was hampered by injuries, resulting in Tottenham's worst-ever Premier League finish at 17th, one spot above relegation, with the most defeats and lowest points tally in a single season. This poor performance raised speculation about his dismissal. Despite the league struggles, Postecoglou led Tottenham to their first trophy in 17 years by defeating Manchester United 1–0 in the 2025 UEFA Europa League final on 21 May 2025, their first title since the 2007–08 Football League Cup and their first European trophy since the 1983–84 UEFA Cup. The victory earned a league phase spot in the 2025–26 UEFA Champions League and the right to play against the 2024–25 UEFA Champions League winners for the 2025 UEFA Super Cup, making Postecoglou the first Australian and first Greek manager to win a European competition. During the Europa League victory parade on 23 May, he openly campaigned to return for the next season, stating "all the best TV series, season three is better than season two." However, on 6 June, exactly two years after his appointment, he was relieved of his duties as Tottenham's head coach. On 9 September 2025, he was announced as head coach of Nottingham Forest, signing a two-year contract as successor to Nuno Espírito Santo. He lost his first game as Forest manager 3–0 to Arsenal, followed by defeats to Swansea City in the League Cup and to Sunderland and Newcastle United in the Premier League, and a loss to FC Midtjylland in the Europa League, with draws against Burnley and Real Betis, resulting in a winless start in his first seven fixtures—the worst start by a Forest manager in over a century—and his job security being questioned after less than a month. After a 3–0 home defeat by Chelsea on 18 October 2025 that dropped the team into the relegation zone, Forest announced Postecoglou's departure just 18 minutes after the final whistle, making him the shortest-reigning manager in the club's history. Evangelos Marinakis had already left his seat when the team was 2–0 down. Postecoglou won none of his 8 games in charge, drawing 2 and losing 6, with a managerial reign of just 39 days—the second shortest in English Premier League history, only behind Sam Allardyce's 30-day tenure at Leeds United—and was replaced by Sean Dyche.
